name: OSIC Pulmonary Fibrosis Progression 1st Place — Multimodal Quantile Regression with CT Image Features
summary: Predict lung function decline in pulmonary fibrosis patients using EfficientNet-B5 CT scan feature extraction, tabular feature engineering of baseline FVC and temporal deltas, and MLP quantile regression predicting 20th/50th/80th percentiles for confidence-aware FVC forecasting.
dejargonized_summary: Predict how a patient's lung capacity will change over time by combining features from their CT scan images with clinical measurements, training a neural network that outputs both the predicted value and how uncertain it is.

inputs.name: ct_scans
inputs.constraints: 3D CT scan volumes per patient. Variable slice counts.

inputs.name: patient_metadata
inputs.constraints: Patient metadata: age, sex, smoking status.

outputs.name: fvc_predictions
outputs.constraints: Predicted FVC values with confidence intervals at future timepoints.

planning_constraints.subject: image_features_before_concatenation
planning_constraints.statement: CT image feature extraction must precede feature concatenation.
planning_constraints.rationale: Image features are a required input to the concatenation step that assembles the complete feature vector.
planning_constraints.source_reference: OSIC Pulmonary Fibrosis 1st place solution writeup

planning_constraints.subject: quantile_before_confidence
planning_constraints.statement: Quantile regression training must precede confidence interval postprocessing.
planning_constraints.rationale: Confidence intervals are derived from the spread between predicted percentiles; these percentiles must be predicted first.
planning_constraints.source_reference: OSIC Pulmonary Fibrosis 1st place solution writeup

stages.name: Image Feature Extraction
stages.description: Pass CT scan volumes through a pretrained EfficientNet-B5 backbone to produce compact 1D feature vectors per patient, using PyTorch.
stages.dejargonized_description: Use a pretrained image recognition model to convert 3D CT scans into a compact numerical summary that captures lung structure information.

inputs.name: ct_scans
inputs.constraints: 3D CT volumes. Preprocessed to standard resolution.

outputs.name: image_features
outputs.constraints: Shape (N_patients, D). Dense feature vectors from EfficientNet-B5 penultimate layer.

preconditions: CT scans are preprocessed to compatible input format for EfficientNet.
guarantees: Each patient receives a fixed-length feature vector regardless of scan volume size.
family_notes: EfficientNet-B5 pretrained on ImageNet, applied slice-by-slice or via 3D adaptation.
Feature vectors are extracted from the global average pooling layer.

stages.name: Tabular Feature Engineering
stages.description: Calculate baseline FVC values, temporal deltas from baseline measurement date to prediction targets, and derived features from patient metadata using pandas.
stages.dejargonized_description: Compute derived numerical features from clinical data, such as time elapsed since first measurement and starting lung capacity.

outputs.name: tabular_features
outputs.constraints: Engineered tabular features including baseline FVC, temporal deltas, encoded demographics.

preconditions: Metadata and FVC measurements share a common patient identifier.
guarantees: All temporal features are computed relative to a consistent baseline.

stages.name: Feature Concatenation
stages.description: Combine tabular metadata features with CT image feature vectors into a single input vector per patient-timepoint using numpy.
stages.dejargonized_description: Merge the image-derived features with the clinical features into one combined input for the prediction model.

inputs.name: image_features
inputs.constraints: EfficientNet feature vectors, one per patient.

outputs.name: combined_features
outputs.constraints: Concatenated feature vectors combining image and tabular data.

preconditions: Image and tabular features are aligned by patient ID.
guarantees: Output contains both modalities for every patient-timepoint.

stages.name: Quantile Regression Training
stages.description: Train an MLP with custom Quantile Loss function predicting the 20th, 50th, and 80th percentiles of FVC at each future timepoint, using PyTorch.
stages.dejargonized_description: Train a neural network that predicts not just the expected lung capacity but also optimistic and pessimistic estimates, giving a natural measure of uncertainty.

outputs.name: quantile_predictions
outputs.constraints: Shape (N, 3). Predicted 20th, 50th, and 80th percentile FVC values.

preconditions: Combined features are available for all patient-timepoints.
guarantees: Three quantile predictions per sample. 20th <= 50th <= 80th by construction of the loss.
family_notes: Quantile loss: L_q(y, y_hat) = max(q*(y - y_hat), (q-1)*(y - y_hat)).
Three separate output heads or a single model with composite loss.

stages.name: Confidence Interval Postprocessing
stages.description: Calculate confidence intervals from the spread between predicted 20th and 80th percentiles, producing the final FVC prediction (50th percentile) with uncertainty bounds using numpy.
stages.dejargonized_description: Convert the three percentile predictions into a final answer with error bars, where wider spread between optimistic and pessimistic predictions means more uncertainty.

outputs.name: fvc_predictions
outputs.constraints: Final FVC predictions with confidence intervals. Columns: patient_id, week, FVC, Confidence.

preconditions: Quantile predictions maintain ordering: q20 <= q50 <= q80.
guarantees: Confidence values are positive and reflect prediction uncertainty.
family_notes: Competition metric (modified Laplace log-likelihood) explicitly rewards well-calibrated confidence intervals.
Confidence = (q80 - q20) scaled by a learned or fixed constant.

edges.provenance: Dense image features from EfficientNet-B5 applied to CT scans.
Engineered tabular features from patient metadata and FVC measurements.
Multimodal feature vector combining image and tabular data.

audit.rationale: 1st place Kaggle OSIC Pulmonary Fibrosis solution. Multimodal regression combining CT image features with clinical tabular data via quantile regression for uncertainty-aware FVC prediction.
audit.dejargonized_summary: Predict lung function decline with uncertainty by combining CT scan image analysis with clinical data in a neural network that outputs confidence intervals.
provenance_notes: Source: Kaggle OSIC Pulmonary Fibrosis Progression competition (2020), 1st place solution
uncertainty_notes: EfficientNet-B5 features may not capture all relevant CT scan pathology.
Quantile crossing (q20 > q50) can occur without explicit monotonicity constraints.
Confidence interval calibration depends on the distribution of FVC trajectories in the training set.

references.title: OSIC Pulmonary Fibrosis 1st Place Solution
